Sarah —

Thanks for sending this over and for the specific asks. I'm looping in Mina (Privacy) and Marissa (Solutions) so we can give you both the legal attestation and the operational appendix. High-level answers below; formal attestation and a technical appendix are attached.

Summary (short):
- Redwood does not use customer-provided content to train our public or internal model weights, nor to create derivative models, for Hosted and Dedicated customers unless a customer explicitly opts in via a documented agreement.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments: customer has full control over model training — Redwood does not access customer content in private deployments unless explicitly configured to.
- Retention and purge: active content is retained per the contract. Operational snapshots/backups and debug artifacts follow the timeline below (also in attached appendix):
  * KV cache / ephemeral inference caches: evicted within 24–72 hours by default; not persisted beyond short-term debug windows.
  * Live request logs & telemetry: retained for 30 days by default, can be reduced via contract.
  * Persistent backups / snapshots (region DR copies): rotated every 30 days; encrypted; retained for up to 90 days for restore and disaster recovery unless otherwise contractually agreed.
  * Archive/SLA snapshots: if a customer requests full purge, we will remove live content and trigger a deletion workflow; final purge from backups and DR copies completes within 90 days from the deletion request (exceptions described below).

Exceptions & notes:
- Aggregated, non-identifiable product telemetry (metrics and usage aggregates) may be retained beyond these windows for product analytics; that telemetry does not include customer text and is not used to train model weights.
- Temporary debug snapshots (created only for specific incidents, with access controls and short TTLs) are scoped in the attached appendix.

Next steps:
1) Attached: redwood-nontraining-attestation.pdf (one-page attestation you can include in the SOW).
2) Attached: data-lifecycle-appendix.pdf — ops runbook with purge steps and roles (Engineering, Legal, Customer Ops).
3) If procurement wants contractual language, below is wording you can paste into the SOW:

-----Suggested contract language (start)-----
Redwood Inference Attestation: Redwood will not use Customer Content to train or improve Redwood's public or shared model weights, nor to create derivative models, without the Customer's explicit, documented consent. Redwood will implement the deletion/purge workflow described in the attached Data Lifecycle Appendix. Upon receipt of a Customer deletion request, Redwood will remove Customer Content from live stores within 7 days and will complete deletion from backups and regionally replicated snapshots within 90 days, with reasonable exceptions for restore operations. Aggregated non-identifying telemetry may be retained for product analytics and is not used for model training.
-----Suggested contract language (end)-----

Sarah —

Adding a few controls and clarifications from the privacy and compliance perspective:

- Attestation & signing: We can provide a signed attestation (PDF) and add an email-confirmed attestation as an appendix to the SOW. Our standard attestation confirms non-use for model training for Hosted and Dedicated; for Private deployments we will document access controls and confirm no Redwood access unless configured.
- Backups & DR: Backups are encrypted at rest (KMS-managed). Backup retention is a configurable parameter in the contract; default is 90 days. If FinnovA needs a shorter retention window, we can include a contractual commitment to 30 days with an SLA.
- Purge mechanics: The deletion workflow performs logical deletes (mark-for-delete) immediately, physical deletion from live stores in up to 7 days, and background purge from backups/replicas within 90 days. We keep an audit trail (deletion job IDs, timestamps) which we can provide to customers upon request.
- Logs & snapshots: Debug snapshots for triage are scoped to authorized on-call engineers and are auto-rotated; they are explicitly excluded from training data.
- Product telemetry: We only ingest aggregated, non-identifiable metrics for product analytics. If FinnovA requires a complete opt-out, we can include an opt-out flag in the provisioning flow for that customer tenant.

If procurement needs a technical contact for the appendix, Marissa will own that. Happy to sign the attestation and discuss any carve-outs required by your legal team.
